clue.text: Drink manufacturer that is grasping yet accepted by thirsty

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken inside it, so the inner pieces sit within the word for thirsty

parts.note: thirsty means dry

indicators.note: the abbreviation for 'that is' holds the next word in its grip, wrapping round it

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'
still can mean yet, as in 'still, it worked'

explanation.surface: A drinks maker is greedy, yet still welcomed by people who are thirsty.
explanation.definitionFit: A distillery is a plant that produces spirits such as whisky, so it manufactures drink.

clue.text: Orchestral section lacks right instrument

indicators.note: the orchestral section is missing a letter, so lacking signals taking it away

parts.note: the brass is the section of trumpets, horns and trombones

explanation.surface: An orchestra's section is missing the right instrument for the piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks' removes R from BRASS. 'Orchestral section' looks like the definition, but the definition is 'instrument' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass is a low-pitched instrument, such as a double bass or bass guitar.

clue.text: A young man finally starred in panto

parts.note: a lad is a young man

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word starred

explanation.surface: A young lad ended up with the starring role in a pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: Panto, short for pantomime, is a British Christmas family theatre show based on fairy tales; Aladdin is a classic one.
explanation.definitionFit: Aladdin is one of the best-known traditional British pantomime stories, so it names a panto by example.

clue.text: Tall vase has broken mug in kiln

indicators.note: the vase breaks into the other word, splitting it open and sitting inside

parts.note: mug is slang for face
an urn is a tall vase

explanation.surface: A tall vase has smashed a mug inside the pottery kiln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has broken' signals the vase going inside the other word. 'mug' is slang for a face, not a cup, despite the pottery setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln and a furnace are both enclosed chambers heated to very high temperatures.

clue.text: Shocking revelation cut short more than one big show

indicators.note: cutting something short trims its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an ...é is a report revealing a scandal

explanation.surface: A scandalous exposé was stopped early, much like several big exhibitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the last E of EXPOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An expo is a large exhibition, so the plural means more than one big show.

clue.text: Admit too many to where air displays can't take place

definitions.meaning: to let in more people than a place can hold

definitions.text: where air displays can't take place
definitions.meaning: split as two words, over a crowd: aerobatic displays may not fly above the spectators

explanation.walkthrough: Air-show rules forbid display aircraft from flying over the crowd, so the second definition is the answer split into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcrowd is to pack a space with more people than it should hold, which is admitting too many.

clue.text: One can't know why the votes aren't counted

definitions.meaning: an idiom meaning it is impossible to predict
tellers count votes, so if votes go uncounted there is nobody doing the telling

explanation.walkthrough: In Parliament the MPs who count votes in a division are called tellers; 'telling' is the counting.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses that nobody can predict or be sure of something, matching one being unable to know.

clue.text: Irregular bet incriminates leading politician

indicators.note: irregular says the letters are out of their proper order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: An improper wager lands a senior politician in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irregular' rearranges BET and INCRIMINATES, fifteen letters, into the two-word answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet minister is a senior government member in the British system, hence a leading politician.

clue.text: Able to stretch out beside quiet part of garden

indicators.note: beside places one piece next to the other; here the quiet sign comes first

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
something rubbery is elastic and can be stretched

explanation.surface: A gardener is able to stretch out next to a quiet corner of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beside' only says the two pieces sit side by side; here the quiet sign comes first. 'stretch out' suggests lounging in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrubbery is an area of a garden planted with shrubs.

clue.text: Potato cake served initially in bread

indicators.note: the opening letter is placed inside the word for bread

parts.note: roti is an Indian flatbread

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of served

explanation.surface: A potato cake is first served in a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes S from 'served'; 'in' puts it inside ROTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Rösti is a Swiss dish of grated potato fried into a flat cake.

clue.text: Flavouring I understand must be used in conjunction

indicators.note: the first words have to go inside the word for a conjunction, so they are placed within it

parts.note: and is the commonest conjunction in grammar
to see is to understand, as in 'I see'

explanation.surface: A cook says she knows the flavouring must be used together with something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be used in' places the phrase for 'I understand' inside the conjunction; the surface's 'in conjunction' means together, a false lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Aniseed is the seed of the anise plant, used to give food and drink a liquorice taste.

clue.text: Ornamental plant a naturalist gathers

indicators.note: the phrase gathers the answer into itself, holding it among its letters

explanation.surface: A nature lover collects an ornamental plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ornamental plant' looks like the definition, but 'plant' starts the run of letters that 'gathers' collects: pLANT A NAturalist. The definition is just 'Ornamental', used as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Lantana is a flowering shrub grown in gardens for show, so it is an ornamental, a noun meaning a decorative plant.

clue.text: One may find a landlady here does mine

definitions.text: One may find a landlady here
definitions.meaning: lodgings rented in someone's house, where a landlady looks after the tenant

explanation.walkthrough: Digs is British slang for rented lodgings, classically run by a landlady.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs is informal for lodgings with a landlady, and as a verb it means excavates, as mining does.

clue.text: Again timetable is held secure for distribution

indicators.note: letters handed out for distribution are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A rearranged timetable is kept safe before being handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for distribution' rearranges HELD and SECURE; 'is' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To reschedule is to timetable something a second time, setting a new date.

clue.text: Face East Enders' frantic investigation to determine truth

parts.note: the dial is the face of a clock or watch

indicators.note: as said by East Enders, Cockneys, who drop the H at the start of words

parts.note: hectic means frantic

explanation.surface: A face from the soap EastEnders is involved in a frantic inquiry into the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East Enders' is split: 'East' gives E, and 'Enders'' signals the London Cockney habit of dropping the H at the start of words. EastEnders is also a British TV soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialectic is the philosophical method of seeking truth through reasoned argument and debate.

clue.text: Small instrument needing tuning down a bit

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
the harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A small instrument needs its tuning lowered slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: A note that is sharp is slightly too high in pitch, so it needs tuning down a little.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, sharp means slightly above the correct pitch, so the player must lower it a touch.

clue.text: Vague brides incline to be all over the place

indicators.text: to be all over the place
indicators.note: being all over the place means scattered in disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Uncertain brides tend to be disorganised on the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be all over the place' rearranges BRIDES and INCLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indiscernible cannot be made out clearly, so it is vague or imperceptible.

clue.text: US politician left most of soft drink in pub

indicators.note: the shortened drink is placed inside the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: most of a word means it loses its last letter

parts.note: cola is a fizzy soft drink

explanation.surface: An American politician left most of his cola in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the final letter of the drink and 'in' places what remains inside the pub word. The surface 'left' reads as a verb, but is the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham Lincoln was the 16th US president, a famous American politician.

clue.text: Ponder resistance and choose to embrace force

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: the word for choose takes the next piece into its arms, enclosing it

parts.note: to elect is to choose
F is the symbol for force in physics

explanation.surface: Think about resisting, and decide whether to welcome force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to embrace' puts F inside ELECT, after R.
explanation.definitionFit: To reflect is to think carefully about something, the same as to ponder.

clue.text: Expert in figures in a haze about military organisation

indicators.note: about means going round, so the haze phrase surrounds the organisation

parts.note: mist is a haze
NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, a military alliance

explanation.surface: An accountant expert in figures is in a fog about a military organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the hazy phrase round the alliance. 'figures' suggests numbers, but here it means human bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: An anatomist studies the structure of the body, so is an expert in human figures.

clue.text: Was sick with weight loss drug

indicators.note: loss of the weight letter means it is taken away from the word

parts.note: spewed means vomited, was sick

explanation.surface: Someone was sick after taking a weight-loss drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loss' takes W out of SPEWED. 'weight loss' reads as one phrase but splits across two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed is slang for amphetamine, a stimulant drug.

clue.text: Lack of co-operation redesigning an electric car

indicators.note: redesigning reshapes the letters of the phrase into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Engineers stubbornly refuse to help with redesigning an electric car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redesigning' rearranges AN ELECTRIC CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Recalcitrance is stubborn refusal to obey or comply, a lack of co-operation.

clue.text: Yours truly elevated to prevent top man taking place on board

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a word lifts it upwards so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: yours truly means the speaker, me
to bar is to prevent
a king is the top man

explanation.surface: I was promoted to stop the boss from taking a seat on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' reverses ME to EM, as this is a down entry. 'taking place on board' suggests a company board, but means boarding a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Embarking means going aboard a ship or aircraft, taking one's place on board.

clue.text: A regiment prepared to shoot

indicators.note: prepared means made ready by rearranging, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A regiment is ready to open fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges A REGIMENT. 'shoot' looks military, but it means a plant sprouting.
explanation.definitionFit: A seed germinates when it begins to sprout, so to germinate is to shoot as plants do.

clue.text: One needing sole contact for power transmission

definitions.text: One needing sole contact for power transmission

parts.words: One needing sole contact for power transmission
parts.note: a foot pedal driving a machine such as an old sewing machine works only when the sole of a shoe presses it

explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' suggests the fish or 'only', but it is the underside of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot-operated lever that drives a machine, so power passes through the sole pressing it.

clue.text: Blissful days in Scilly Is going over without either son

indicators.note: the letter for days sits within the rest
going over is turning over, so the letters are read backwards
without means lacking, so both letters for son are dropped

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, and either means both of the two S letters
D is the abbreviation for days, as in diaries

explanation.surface: Days spent in the Isles of Scilly are perfect, travelling without either son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without either son' drops both S letters from SCILLYIS to give CILLYI; 'going over' reverses it to IYLLIC; 'in' puts D inside. The Isles of Scilly are islands off Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Idyllic describes a peaceful, perfect scene, which is blissful.

clue.text: Pulls up area of grass

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom, so it runs backwards

parts.note: draws means pulls, as a horse draws a cart

explanation.surface: Someone pulls up a patch of grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses DRAWS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A sward is an expanse of short grass, such as turf.

clue.text: Total confusion in United supporters' uprising

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading from bottom to top, so both pieces run backwards

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names
fans are supporters

explanation.surface: There is total chaos when a football club's fans riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' reverses U FANS. Snafu is a slang acronym for a chaotic mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A snafu is a chaotic, badly botched situation, total confusion.
